summary: Objects are no longer linked to the scene directly. Link them to a collection (the scene's master collection or any child collection). scene.objects.link raises AttributeError in 2.80 and later.
Selection is per view layer since 2.80, so the boolean property Object.select was removed. Use obj.select_set(True) to select and obj.select_get() to read the state.
The active object belongs to the view layer since 2.80 (LayerObjects.active), not the scene. Set it through context.view_layer.objects.active.
Object.hide was split: hide_viewport disables the object in all viewports, hide_set() hides it in the current view layer only (the eye icon). hide_render is unchanged.
after:
obj.hide_set(True)        # per view layer (eye icon)
obj.hide_viewport = True  # global viewport disable

summary: scene.update() was removed with the new dependency graph. Call view_layer.update() to re-evaluate after changing data.
Matrix, vector and quaternion multiplication uses the @ operator since 2.80. The * operator now means element-wise multiplication, so old code silently computes the wrong result instead of failing.
Passing a context override dict as the first positional argument to an operator was deprecated in 3.2 and removed in 4.0. Wrap the call in context.temp_override(...) instead.

Node group sockets are managed through NodeTree.interface since 4.0. inputs.new/outputs.new/remove/move were removed. socket_type accepts only base socket type names, e.g. NodeSocketFloat, not NodeSocketFloatFactor.
The Principled BSDF was rewritten in 4.0. The 'Emission' color socket is now 'Emission Color'; strength stays 'Emission Strength'. Indexing inputs['Emission'] raises KeyError in 4.0 and later.

Principled BSDF 4.0 socket renames: Specular → Specular IOR Level, Subsurface → Subsurface Weight, Transmission → Transmission Weight, Sheen → Sheen Weight, Coat → Coat Weight. Specular Tint changed from float to color.
The 'Subsurface Color' socket was removed from the Principled BSDF in 4.0; subsurface scattering uses Base Color. There is no replacement socket.
Fixed 32 bone layers and bone groups were replaced by named bone collections in 4.0. Create with armature.collections.new(name) and assign with collection.assign(bone) or bone.collections.
The Python OBJ add-on was removed in 4.0 after the C++ exporter shipped in 3.x. Use bpy.ops.wm.obj_export; the option names differ (e.g. export_selected_objects instead of use_selection).
OBJ import moved to bpy.ops.wm.obj_import in 4.0. Same change applies to PLY: import_mesh.ply/export_mesh.ply became wm.ply_import/wm.ply_export.
Mesh.calc_normals() was removed in 4.0. Normals are computed on demand; read them via vertex.normal, polygon.normal or Mesh.vertex_normals / polygon_normals without calling anything first.

use_auto_smooth and auto_smooth_angle were removed in 4.1. Face-corner normals are used automatically when smooth and flat faces are mixed. Angle-based smoothing is done by the operator bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth_by_angle(angle=...) (named shade_auto_smooth in 4.1, renamed in 4.2; both names work in 4.5 and 5.0), which shade-smooths the faces and marks the boolean 'sharp_edge' edge attribute. It works on the active/selected objects and adds NO modifier. There is no modifier type 'SMOOTH_BY_ANGLE': obj.modifiers.new(name, 'SMOOTH_BY_ANGLE') raises TypeError. The 'Smooth by Angle' node-group asset from the Essentials library can be added as a geometry-nodes modifier via bpy.ops.object.modifier_add_node_group, but the operator is the simple form.
after:
import math
obj = bpy.data.objects['Cube']
bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = obj
obj.select_set(True)
bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth_by_angle(angle=math.radians(30))  # 4.2+; sets use_smooth + 'sharp_edge' attribute, no modifier

summary: The split-normal helper trio was removed in 4.1. Read per-corner normals from the read-only Mesh.corner_normals collection; set custom normals with normals_split_custom_set().
EEVEE was replaced by EEVEE Next in 4.2 and the engine identifier changed to BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT. Assigning 'BLENDER_EEVEE' raises TypeError in 4.2–4.5. Note: 5.0 renamed it back to BLENDER_EEVEE.
In 5.0 the EEVEE identifier reverted from BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT to BLENDER_EEVEE. Scripts that must run on both 4.2 LTS and 5.0 should pick the identifier from bpy.app.version.

EEVEE Next replaced blend_method ('OPAQUE', 'BLEND', 'HASHED', 'CLIP') with surface_render_method ('DITHERED' or 'BLENDED'). show_transparent_back became use_transparency_overlap and use_screen_refraction became use_raytrace_refraction.

Shadow casting was de-duplicated between Cycles and EEVEE in 4.2: light.cycles.cast_shadow moved to light.use_shadow. Motion blur settings likewise moved from scene.cycles / scene.eevee to scene.render.
4.5 added a third boolean solver, 'MANIFOLD' (fastest, requires manifold meshes). Valid values in 4.5: 'FAST', 'EXACT', 'MANIFOLD'; default 'EXACT'. 'MANIFOLD' is a TypeError on 4.2 and earlier.
before: mod.solver = "EXACT"  # 4.2: only FAST or EXACT exist

summary: The boolean solver enum value 'FAST' was renamed to 'FLOAT' in 5.0 (BooleanModifier and the mesh boolean operators). Valid values in 5.0: 'FLOAT', 'EXACT', 'MANIFOLD'. 'EXACT' is unchanged and safe across all versions.

4.4 introduced slotted actions. Action.fcurves, groups and id_root still work as a legacy API but are deprecated; assigning animation_data.action may not auto-assign a slot, so set animation_data.action_slot explicitly.
after:
action = obj.animation_data.action
slot = obj.animation_data.action_slot
bag = action.layers[0].strips[0].channelbag(slot, ensure=True)
fc = bag.fcurves.new("location", index=0)

summary: The legacy Action API (fcurves, groups, id_root) was removed in 5.0. Get the channelbag for the slot with bpy_extras.anim_utils.action_ensure_channelbag_for_slot(action, slot) and use its fcurves. The keyframe_insert 'action_group' parameter was renamed 'group_name'.
after:
from bpy_extras import anim_utils
bag = anim_utils.action_ensure_channelbag_for_slot(action, obj.animation_data.action_slot)
for fc in bag.fcurves:
    print(fc.data_path)

summary: All video-sequencer 'Sequence' types were renamed to 'Strip' in 4.4 (ImageSequence → ImageStrip, MovieSequence → MovieStrip, ...). The old property names are deprecated aliases.

Compositor node trees became regular node-group datablocks in 5.0. scene.node_tree and scene.use_nodes are gone; assign a node group to scene.compositing_node_group. The File Output node's file_slots became file_output_items and base_path split into directory and file_name.
Lamps were renamed to Lights in 2.80: the datablock collection is bpy.data.lights, the type is bpy.types.Light, the operator is object.light_add.
Duplication became instancing in 2.80: dupli_type -> instance_type, dupli_group -> instance_collection, and the enum value is 'COLLECTION' instead of 'GROUP'.
The 3D cursor became a struct in 2.80: scene.cursor.location (and cursor.rotation_euler) replaces scene.cursor_location.

Principled BSDF 4.0 socket renames: 'Subsurface' -> 'Subsurface Weight' (likewise 'Transmission' -> 'Transmission Weight', 'Sheen' -> 'Sheen Weight', 'Clearcoat' -> 'Coat Weight'). Verified in 3.6.23 vs 4.2.23.
In 5.0 new_effect() takes `length` instead of `frame_end`; passing frame_end raises TypeError (invalid keyword argument). Verified in 5.0.1 vs 4.5.14.

replacement: NodeGroupOutput with an Image output socket on the node group interface
summary: 5.0 compositor trees are node groups: the Composite output node is gone (nodes.new raises 'Node type CompositorNodeComposite undefined'); the final image is whatever is wired into the Group Output node's 'Image' interface socket. A fresh CompositorNodeTree is empty. Verified in 5.0.1.
